newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland should delay EMU entry, await UK move - broker.
newsitem.headline: Ireland should delay EMU entry, await UK move - broker.

text.p: Ireland should postpone its participation in Economic and monetary union (EMU) until Britain decides to join, Davy stockbrokers economist Jim O'Leary said on Thursday.

"We should postpone our participation until the UK decides to come on board and, in the meantime, pursue an exchange rate policy similar to the one that has been in place over the past three-and-a-half years," O'Leary told graduates at University College Cork.
O'Leary said this strategy would preserve the benefits that flow from retaining monetary policy autonomy and provide cover against the risks that relinquishing such autonomy would entail.
It would also provide Ireland with an opportunity to monitor the progress and performance of the monetary union from the outside, he said.

"There is after all no guarantee that the project will be a success, and there are several reasons to believe that it will be beset by difficulties at least in the early years," O'Leary said. "If it was not successful, it would be better to be out than in."
O'Leary said the risks that attach to joining the single currency at the outset are of an entirely different order to those that attach to postponing membership.
"A decision to join cannot be reversed; a decision to postpone joining can be reviewed at any time."

He said another reason for postponing and maintaining Ireland's current exchange rate policy of a managed float was that it had been associated with a period of exceptionally good performance by the Irish economy.
"It is hard to believe that that performance has not been greatly helped by the currency policy in place in 1993."
"Equally it is hard to believe that that performance will not be put in jeopardy by joining a single currency whose other members account for no more than 30 percent of our trade," O'Leary said.
